question: Does whole-video aggregation hide heterogeneous signed error preferences in existing R7 full-restoration flow fields?
input: Original R7D1 A/B full-flow tensors and DQ targets, after the R12 saved-operand SHA audit; sources 00/05/10/15 are all previously development-exposed.
partitions_fixed_before_new_tensor_analy: One selected historical restoration per entire source video
One selected historical restoration per native latent frame (21 frames)
One selected historical restoration per original output token (1x2x2 latent patch, 64 flow values, 31668 tokens)
objective: FP64 squared error against the same original DQ flow; sum all components with equal source weighting and no pixel/source/partition selection.

opposing_predictions.source_only_preference: Finer partitions add little reduction beyond the whole-source hindsight choice.
opposing_predictions.heterogeneous_direction_preference: Finer partitions materially lower the error of a post-action output mosaic even when whole-source preferences nearly cancel.

required_checks: Original file and decoded tensor SHA/shape checks; no new quantization or model execution
Native-patch and frame losses each sum to the original whole-flow SSE
Best fixed loss >= source-mosaic loss >= frame-mosaic loss >= native-token-mosaic loss
Report every source and the exact same A/B action outputs, with no tuning
interpretation_boundary: This is offline target-dependent stitching of ALREADY COMPUTED global restoration outputs. It is NOT the result of executing spatially mixed FFN actions, NOT a bound on such execution, NOT R12 equal-budget conditional action headroom, NOT a deployable selector, and NOT video quality. Both original forwards and the DQ target were needed to construct it.
stop: Any identity, finite-value or partition-additivity failure stops the audit. A large mosaic benefit may motivate a distinct tile-action counterfactual, but cannot authorize a model run or widen the old q/pool search.
